summary: Escaped characters in Okta service metadata claim cause RBAC parse failures for service-bot sessions
description:
Issue summary:
A subset of service-bot sessions are failing to acquire RBAC roles when signing in via Okta SSO. The auth stack reports a JSON parse error when parsing the service metadata claim. The claim payload contains escaped sequences (e.g., backslash-escaped quotes and control characters) that the RBAC parser does not tolerate.

Impact:
- ~12% of service-bot login attempts into internal consoles return 403 or result in ephemeral session creation failures.
- Affects internal automation that relies on service-bot tokens (deploy hooks, scheduled oncall runbooks).
- Customers not impacted (internal-support only) but oncall and infra automation reliability degraded.

Environment:
- Production (us-west cluster), observed since 2026-03-09 03:20 UTC.
- Okta -> proxy -> console-auth -> rbac-service flow.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Trigger service-bot login via Okta app (service-bot is provisioned via JIT).
2) Inspect SAML/OIDC assertion: service.metadata claim contains escaped JSON string (e.g. "owner": "team\"infra\"").
3) auth-proxy logs a parse exception when passing the claim to rbac-service.

Observed logs (snippets):
- auth-proxy: "Failed to unmarshal service.metadata: invalid escape sequence at offset 137"
- rbac-service: "role mapping aborted — parse error, rawClaim='\"owner\":\"team\\\"infra\\\"\"'"
- Okta system logs show the assertion delivered as application/x-www-form-urlencoded encoded JSON in the claim.

Initial hypothesis:
The Okta provisioning flow is embedding an already-escaped JSON blob into the claim string. When the proxy attempts to re-interpret the claim as JSON it encounters double-escaped characters, leading to a parse failure. Alternate hypothesis: an encoding mismatch during assertion transformation in our SSO adapter (URL-decoding vs JSON-unescaping).
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 10:12 - Reproduced locally with a synthetic assertion that includes backslash-escaped quotes; parser fails with same exception.

Examined Okta app mapping: attribute maps 'service.metadata' to a custom profile field containing JSON serialized server-side. Mapping looks unchanged since last deploy (no rollouts around 2026-03-09).
Auth-proxy versions: 1.4.7 (prod). RBAC service version: 2.9.1. No recent changes in parsing libraries, but proxy uses a JSON library that treats backslashes literally unless explicitly unescaped.
Cross-checked SAML vs OIDC assertions: both show escaped payloads when the source metadata includes nested JSON strings (we have a handful of older service-bots still using legacy metadata encoding).
Threat model: malformed claim could be exploited to bypass role mapping if parsing were coerced — low immediate risk but should be hardened.
Telemetry: spike in parse exceptions from 2026-03-09 03:22 UTC; 18 distinct service-bot client IDs affected, all created before 2025-10-01.
comments: Maya Thompson (Reporter) 2026-03-10: Noticed this after a scheduled deploy didn't run; our deploy hook reported 403 from the console API. Opening ticket so SRE can triage.

Evan Brooks (Assignee) 2026-03-10: Assigned. Initial reproduce and logs collected. Suspect double-escaping on older service-bot profiles. Will attempt quick mitigation in proxy to tolerate escaped JSON.
SRE Oncall 2026-03-11: Applied rate-limited mitigation to auth-proxy in us-west: added a tolerant-unescape wrapper before RBAC parse. Monitoring for regressions.
Platform Eng 2026-03-12: Confirmed mitigation reduces 403s from ~12% to ~1.2% for affected clients. Preparing a proper fix in auth-proxy to normalize claim decoding. PR reference posted below.
Maya Thompson 2026-03-14: Please include a short runbook entry for teams that onboard older service-bots so they understand encoding requirements.
workaround: Deploy temporary tolerant-unescape layer in auth-proxy (done 2026-03-11, us-west) that attempts JSON unescape if initial parse fails. This reduces impact but is not ideal for correctness.
resolution: Patch created to normalize Okta claim decoding in auth-proxy; PR opened (github.com/redwood/auth-proxy/pull/862). Plan: merge after tests, rollout canary to us-west on 2026-03-16, followed by global rollout. Post-fix actions: update onboarding doc and add validation to service-bot provisioning to prevent double-escaped metadata.
next_steps: Review and merge PR 862 (auth-proxy) — owner: Platform Eng
Canary rollout to us-west during low-traffic window 2026-03-16 02:00-04:00 UTC
Add CI check to catch double-escaped metadata during service-bot provisioning
Create a runbook entry and notify infra teams of encoding expectations
